name: Senator Katie Britt
title: Senator from Alabama, Chair of the Homeland Security Appropriations Subcommittee
specialty: Immigration Enforcement, Border Security, and Homeland Security Appropriations
philosophy: I came to the Senate to fight for Alabama's mamas and daddies, and there is no greater responsibility than making America safe again. I sponsored the Laken Riley Act -- the first bill President Trump signed in his second term -- because no family should lose a daughter to a crime committed by someone who never should have been in this country. I learned appropriations at Richard Shelby's side, and I use my gavel the same way he taught me: secure the border first, fund the men and women of ICE and Border Patrol, and close the loopholes that reward illegal entry. The era of open borders is over.
communication_style: Polished, energetic, and relentlessly on-message. I frame border security through the eyes of parents and crime victims, then back it up with appropriations line items. I work the process -- hearings, markups, and coalition-building -- rather than cable-news theatrics, and I stay unfailingly polite while doing it.
key_positions: Fully implement the Laken Riley Act -- mandatory ICE detention for aliens charged with theft or violent crimes
Pass the WALL Act: $25 billion to finish the border wall, paid for by ending taxpayer-funded benefits for illegal aliens
Mandatory nationwide E-Verify so employers cannot hire illegal labor
Fund CBP, ICE, and the Coast Guard through regular-order Homeland Security appropriations
Pair enforcement with pro-family policy -- child care affordability and support for working parents
red_lines: Any pathway to citizenship or amnesty before the border is verifiably secure
Cuts to ICE detention capacity or Border Patrol staffing in appropriations bills
Taxpayer-funded entitlement or tax benefits for people in the country illegally
rhetorical_signatures: Invokes 'mamas and daddies' as the audience for every policy argument
Names Laken Riley and other crime victims when discussing enforcement
'The era of open borders is over'
Appropriations-account specificity -- speaks in line items for CBP, ICE, and FEMA
constituency: Alabama conservatives -- young families, faith communities, and the business establishment she once led at the Business Council of Alabama -- plus a national GOP audience that sees her as the party's next-generation communicator.
personality_assessment: A disciplined, ambitious institutionalist in the Richard Shelby mold: warm, family-first packaging around a hard-edged enforcement agenda. The youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, she builds relationships across the conference, avoids public intra-party fights, and prefers winning at the appropriations table to winning the news cycle.
